methodological_rigor.justification: Case series of 6 relapsed/refractory RUNX1::RUNX1T1+ AML patients treated with olaparib conditioning regimen. LoE 5 (case series). No comparison group. Complete molecular remission achieved in all 6 patients within 3 months. Lacks control arm; small sample size; short follow-up (median 25 months). Single-center experience.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Case series reporting preliminary results of novel conditioning regimen incorporating PARPi for high-risk hematologic malignancy. Potentially relevant for future patient care but insufficient evidence for practice-changing recommendation. Biological rationale (RUNX1::RUNX1T1 HRR deficiency) mechanistically sound but clinically unproven.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods describe treatment protocol and disease monitoring. Results section lacks systematic reporting structure. Individual patient details presented in Tables 1-2. No detailed adverse event grading beyond qualitative description. Data availability not discussed. Limited adherence to STROBE or specialized guidelines.

novelty_literature.justification: First case series of olaparib-containing conditioning for relapsed/refractory RUNX1::RUNX1T1+ AML. Novel combination exploiting identified HRR deficiency. Biological mechanism plausible but not functionally validated in this cohort. Incremental technical advance with preliminary clinical data.

writing_presentation.justification: Methods section detailed for conditioning regimen. Discussion comprehensively reviews PARPi mechanisms and LSC biology. Results section lacks systematic outcome reporting. Some repetition between results and discussion. Figures and tables adequate but limited.

key_strengths: First clinical report of olaparib-enhanced conditioning for RUNX1::RUNX1T1+ AML with mechanistic rationale (HRR deficiency sensitivity)
100% complete molecular remission at 3 months in all 6 patients; durable remission at median 25-month follow-up
Feasible and tolerable conditioning regimen with successful engraftment and manageable GVHD
key_concerns: Case series design without comparison group prohibits causal inference; small sample size (N=6) precludes robust conclusions
Median follow-up 25 months insufficient for long-term hematologic outcomes; no mechanistic validation of PARPi efficacy in vivo
Lack of standardized adverse event reporting; limited toxicity detail compared to systemic criteria
Single-center experience not generalizable; requires prospective validation
chief_reviewer.rationale: Early-phase case series reporting promising preliminary results for novel PARPi-enhanced conditioning in high-risk AML. Biological rationale sound but clinical evidence limited to 6 patients. Tier 4 appropriate for hypothesis-generating preliminary report requiring prospective RCT validation.
